newsitem.title: USA: U.S. publicly calls for dismissal of Bosnia aide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. publicly calls for dismissal of Bosnia aide.

text.p: The United States on Friday publicly called for the dismissal of Bosnian Deputy Defence Minister Hasan Cengic as a condition for delivering $100 million worth of military equipment to Sarajevo.

U.S. officials said privately last week the equipment would not be handed over until Cengic was fired because of his alleged ties with Iran. But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington was now going public because the Bosnian government had not complied.

"The United States has determined that Bosnian Federation Deputy Defense Minister Hasan Cengic personally maintains close ties to Iran," Burns told a news briefing. "He has also obstructed development of the Western-oriented defense structure of the Federation, and has worked against a democratic Federation in general."

"While senior Bosnian officials have assured us that Mr Cengic will be replaced, the United States has decided that the $100 million worth of equipment ... will not be delivered to the Federation until Mr Cengic is relieved of his responsibilities formally and publicly," Burns said.

The bulk of the equipment, which includes tanks, artillery and helicopters, arrived last week by ship at the Croatian port of Ploce, but the vessel has since moved offshore pending resolution of the Cengic dispute.

The equipment is being supplied under a so-called "equip-and-train" program whereby the United States hopes to bring Bosnia's Muslim-Croat Federation up to the military level of its former wartime foe, the Bosnian Serbs.
